newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Israel wants neighbours to share economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Israel wants neighbours to share economic growth.

text.p: Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday Israel was experiencing a technology boom and wanted its neighbours to share in its high-tech future.

Speaking via a satellite link from Lisbon, where he is attending a European security summit, Netanyahu told a conference of business investors in The Hague that Israel saw its economy growing fast because of its highly trained workforce.

"We do not want that future for ourselves alone, we want it for our neighbours, we want it for the Palestinians, we want it for the Egyptians, we want it for the Jordanians," he told delegates to the European Research Center Global Panel.
"This is what we see, not dominion, nor domination but cooperation," he added.

Netanyahu said 80 percent of Israel's exports were technologically-based and this share would probably rise further, with Israel accounting for the highest number of high-tech business startups anywhere outside the United States.
He said this reflected an influx of highly trained people from the former Soviet Union, a strong university base and a stream of well-trained young people emerging from the military.
"The result of these three factors make Israel today a technological boom town. The smartest money in the world is coming," he said.
Netanyahu said a comprehensive privatisation programme would add impetus to Israel's economic push.

"What we intend to do is to privatise and deregulate with a vengeance, we've begun to do that....(in the telecomms industry). "We're going to deregulate many other industries, transport chemicals, everywhere we can," he said.
Netanyahu said his government, which came to power earlier this year amid uncertainty about the Middle East peace process, had not frightened off foreign investment.
"The peace process is not threatened, (and) the smartest money in the world understands that because we've had a 30 percent increase in foreign investment in Israel," he said.
"Israeli companies are investing in capital equipment to the rate of about 12 percent more than they did last year," Netanyahu added.
He said he wanted to see the free flow of goods, services and ideas from Israel to its neighbours.
"I think this is probably far more useful than the heat of rhetoric. This has something for the future, our future and our neighbours' future," said Netanyahu.
